Fetch API engineering notes

Fetch requests should use an abort signal, a manual redirect policy, and explicit response limits. These controls keep failure behavior predictable and prevent a remote server from consuming unbounded time or memory.

The following example demonstrates a small request helper. It includes a timeout and checks the response before reading the body. 

const controller = new AbortController();
const response = await fetch(url, {
  redirect: "manual",
  signal: controller.signal,
});
if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Request failed");

Production code should also validate DNS results, inspect every redirect, reject non-HTML content, and stream the response through a byte counter.

Tests can provide a local HTTP server with deterministic status codes and delayed responses, while production continues to reject loopback targets.

Keeping these responsibilities separate makes both review and maintenance much easier as extraction behavior evolves over time.
